display.description:
RAM configured for the guest operating system. This is the assigned amount, not how much the application is using.

Measurement details:
Memory assigned to the guest. It is not automatically the same as the scheduling request.
display.name: Memory assigned to each VM

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vm_resource_requests{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",resource="memory",unit="bytes",source="guest"}) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"}))), "sre_series", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name"))

display.description:
Memory that the guest can use without swapping, including reclaimable cache. A falling trend can explain application slowdown.

Measurement details:
Memory the guest expects to use without swapping. This comes from the KubeVirt usable_bytes metric.
display.name: Memory available inside each VM

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_memory_usable_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"}))), "sre_series", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name"))

display.description:
CPU use of the busiest selected VM compared with its configured virtual CPUs. If high, open VM Performance to check whether CPU is actually waiting.

Measurement details:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. CPU cores used divided by configured guest vCPUs, not the smaller scheduling request. The VM and namespace filters apply.
display.name: Busiest VM: CPU used

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((last_over_time((topk(1, ((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (rate(kubevirt_vmi_cpu_usage_seconds_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}[5m]))) / ((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (last_over_time(kubevirt_vm_resource_requests{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",resource="cpu",unit="cores",source="domain"}[5m])) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"}[5m])))) * (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (last_over_time(kubevirt_vm_resource_requests{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",resource="cpu",unit="sockets",source="domain"}[5m])) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"}[5m])))) * (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (last_over_time(kubevirt_vm_resource_requests{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",resource="cpu",unit="threads",source="domain"}[5m])) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"}[5m])))) > 0))))[1s:1s] @ end())), "sre_series", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name"))

display.description:
Total capacity of each measured filesystem inside the VM. Compare the same VM and mount point with space used.

Measurement details:
Capacity reported by the guest agent. Reserved blocks and metadata can differ from other disk measurements. Loop-mounted OS images are excluded.
display.name: Size of VM filesystems

display.description:
Highest measured filesystem use inside a VM. Review the named VM and mount point before it fills up. Requires QEMU Guest Agent statistics.

Measurement details:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. Used space divided by filesystem capacity from QEMU Guest Agent. Reserved blocks mean this may differ from df Use%. The VM and namespace filters apply. Loop-mounted OS images are excluded.
display.name: Fullest VM filesystem

display.description:
Percentage used in each measured guest filesystem. A sustained rise toward full requires a guest filesystem review.

Measurement details:
Used space divided by capacity reported by the guest agent. This can differ from df Use%, which excludes reserved blocks. Loop-mounted OS images are excluded.
display.name: VM filesystem space used

display.description:
Bytes used in each reported guest filesystem. The VM operating system sees this space; it differs from Longhorn physical disk usage.

Measurement details:
QEMU Guest Agent reports each mount. This is not PVC allocation or physical space occupied by Longhorn replicas. Loop-mounted OS images are excluded.
display.name: Space used inside VM filesystems

display.description:
Highest memory-use percentage inside a selected VM. This counts memory the guest cannot readily reclaim; check the VM trend before adding RAM.

Measurement details:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. Guest OS total minus available memory, divided by guest OS total. Requires balloon statistics. The VM and namespace filters apply.
display.name: Busiest VM: memory used

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((last_over_time((topk(1, ((clamp_min((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_memory_available_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}[5m])) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"}[5m])))) - (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_memory_usable_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}[5m])) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"}[5m])))), 0)) / (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_memory_available_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}[5m])) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"}[5m]))) > 0))))[1s:1s] @ end())), "sre_series", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name"))

display.description:
Names of running VMs for which guest OS memory statistics were not received. Check guest support and the balloon driver before interpreting other memory charts.

Measurement details:
Running VMs missing total or available memory measurements. Check balloon support. QEMU Guest Agent provides additional filesystem information.
display.name: VMs missing guest memory statistics

display.description:
Memory currently needed inside each selected VM. Compare with available memory; this differs from the VM process memory on the host.

Measurement details:
Guest OS total minus available memory, from KubeVirt balloon statistics. This differs from QEMU memory resident on the host.
display.name: Memory used inside each VM

display.description: Are my virtual machines and their hosts running out of resources?
display.name: What this dashboard tells you

spec.text: **Are my virtual machines and their hosts running out of resources?** Start with the summary, then select a VM to see its memory and disks. VM means the operating system inside the virtual machine; host means the physical Harvester server. Host panels always cover the selected cluster. **No data is not the same as zero.** Use the description icon for measurement details.

display.description:
RAM still available on Harvester servers, including reclaimable cache. Includes every workload on the host, regardless of the VM filter.

Measurement details:
Memory the host considers available for use. VM and namespace filters do not apply.
display.name: Memory available on each host

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((max by (cluster_name,node) (node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",job="sre-node"}) and on (cluster_name) (max by (cluster_name) (label_replace(up{service_name="kubevirt-metrics",k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}, "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)") or label_replace(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}, "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)")))), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "node"))

display.description:
Highest CPU use on a Harvester server. Includes VMs and platform processes, even when a single VM is selected.

Measurement details:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. Five-minute CPU utilization on the virtualization host. It includes VMs and host services. VM and namespace filters do not apply.
display.name: Busiest host: CPU used

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((last_over_time((topk(1, ((1 - avg by (cluster_name,node) (rate(node_cpu_seconds_total{cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",job="sre-node",mode="idle"}[5m]))) and on (cluster_name) (max by (cluster_name) (label_replace(last_over_time(up{service_name="kubevirt-metrics",k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}[5m]), "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)") or label_replace(last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}[5m]), "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)"))))))[1s:1s] @ end())), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "node"))

display.description:
Highest memory use on a Harvester server. Review available memory before starting another VM; host use includes platform overhead.

Measurement details:
Shows the highest value among the selected resources at the end of the time window. The resource is named below. Orange starts at 80%, red at 90%; these are initial reference colors, not proof of an outage. See the historical charts for duration and trend. Host OS total minus available memory, divided by host OS total. It includes VMs and host services. VM and namespace filters do not apply.
display.name: Busiest host: memory used

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((last_over_time((topk(1, (1 - ((max by (cluster_name,node) (last_over_time(node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes{cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",job="sre-node"}[5m])) and on (cluster_name) (max by (cluster_name) (label_replace(last_over_time(up{service_name="kubevirt-metrics",k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}[5m]), "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)") or label_replace(last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}[5m]), "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)")))) / (max by (cluster_name,node) (last_over_time(node_memory_MemTotal_bytes{cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",job="sre-node"}[5m])) and on (cluster_name) (max by (cluster_name) (label_replace(last_over_time(up{service_name="kubevirt-metrics",k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}[5m]), "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)") or label_replace(last_over_time(kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}"}[5m]), "cluster_name", "$1", "k8s_cluster_name", "(.*)"))) > 0)))))[1s:1s] @ end())), "sre_series", " · ", "cluster_name", "node"))

display.description:
Physical host memory used by the VM process, including virtualization overhead. Do not add this to guest memory: they describe different layers of the same VM.

Measurement details:
Resident memory of the process running the VM. It does not directly measure application memory inside the guest.
display.name: VM process memory on the host

spec.query: max by (sre_series) (label_join((max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_memory_resident_bytes{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}"}) and on (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (max by (k8s_cluster_name,namespace,name) (kubevirt_vmi_info{k8s_cluster_name=~"${vm_cluster}",namespace=~"${vm_namespace}",name=~"${vm_name}",phase="running"}))), "sre_series", " · ", "k8s_cluster_name", "namespace", "name"))

display.description:
Number of running VM instances currently reported by KubeVirt. Powered-off VM definitions are not included; compare this with the running list in Harvester.

Measurement details:
Count of unique cluster, namespace and VM names with kubevirt_vmi_info phase="running". Missing input stays empty; it is not a count of stopped VM definitions.
display.name: Running VMs

display.description:
1 means the endpoint answered successfully; 0 means collection failed. Missing lines can mean discovery failed. Check this before trusting an empty chart.

Measurement details:
Per-target KubeVirt and Longhorn scrape status. TLS errors, API discovery permissions, NetworkPolicies or stale CA bundles can break collection even when the collector Pod is Running. Cluster scope; VM filters do not apply.
display.name: Can we collect VM and storage metrics?

display.description:
Average CPU demand in virtual CPU cores. A value of 1 means one core fully occupied over the measurement window, not one configured CPU.

Measurement details:
Five-minute average. A value of 1 means one core used continuously; this value is not in millicores.
display.name: CPU used by each VM (CPU cores)

display.description:
Seconds since the most recent VM identity sample. Compare with the 30-second collection interval; an old sample is a visibility problem.

Measurement details:
Age of the latest VM identity sample. Compare with scrape interval and expected VMs. No data must not be interpreted as healthy or powered off without checking Harvester.
display.name: How old are the VM measurements? (seconds)
